prompt.es: Escucha la charla y resume tres ideas y dos detalles.

answer.text: The lecturer outlined three reasons why cities are planting more trees. According to her, the first reason is that trees cool the streets, and shade can make a street up to five degrees cooler in summer. The second reason is rain: the ground near a tree takes in more water, so there is less flooding after a storm. The third reason is that trees are good for people's minds, because residents who live near trees feel less stressed. She gave one example from a large city, where two thousand trees were planted along one street; after three years, the council reported that the street was noticeably cooler. She went on to give a detail about the costs: a young tree needs water every week for two years, and that costs money. To summarise, the lecturer said that trees are not a quick fix, but they are a good long-term investment.
accepted: The lecturer outlined three reasons why cities are planting more trees. According to her, the first reason is that trees cool the streets, and shade can make a street up to five degrees cooler in summer. The second reason is rain: the ground near a tree takes in more water, so there is less flooding after a storm. The third reason is that trees are good for people's minds, because residents who live near trees feel less stressed. She gave one example from a large city, where two thousand trees were planted along one street; after three years, the council reported that the street was noticeably cooler. She went on to give a detail about the costs: a young tree needs water every week for two years, and that costs money. To summarise, the lecturer said that trees are not a quick fix, but they are a good long-term investment.

The talk was about planting trees in cities. The speaker gave three main ideas. Firstly, trees make streets cooler, by up to 5 degrees in summer, because of the shade. Secondly, trees help when it rains, since the ground takes in water and there is less flooding. Thirdly, people who live near trees seem to feel less stress. As an example, she explained that two thousand trees were planted along one street in a large city, and three years later the street was cooler. She also mentioned a detail about the costs: young trees need water every week for two years, which is expensive for the council. In conclusion, the lecturer said that trees are not a quick solution, but they are a good investment for the future.

feedback.es: El resumen recoge las tres razones, al menos dos detalles de la charla, atribuye las ideas a la conferenciante y cierra con una conclusión.

origin.text: Escucha la charla sobre los árboles en las ciudades (puedes oírla varias veces) y escribe un resumen en inglés de 130 a 250 palabras: tres ideas principales, dos detalles o ejemplos y una frase final. Atribuye las ideas a la conferenciante y no añadas datos que no oigas.
origin.audio: Today I want to talk about why cities are planting more trees. There are three main reasons. First, trees cool the streets. Shade can make a street up to five degrees cooler in summer. Second, trees help with rain. The ground near a tree takes in more water, so there is less flooding after a storm. Third, trees are good for people's minds. Studies suggest that residents who live near trees feel less stressed. One example comes from a large city, where two thousand trees were planted along one street. After three years, the council reported that the street was noticeably cooler. However, trees need care. A young tree needs water every week for two years, and that costs money. In short, trees are not a quick fix, but they are a good long-term investment.

prompt.es: Escucha el episodio y escribe un resumen con una implicación y tu reacción.

answer.text: In this episode, the host asked her guest whether it is better to work from home. According to the guest, it depends. First, many people save about two hours a day because they do not travel, and this is a real benefit. Second, some workers feel lonely and hardly see their colleagues. Third, she said that companies could offer two office days a week, which she described as a good compromise. When the host asked whether working at home is better, she answered that it is not exactly better, which seemed to imply that the answer is not a simple yes. What struck me was that she never said it is easy. To be fair, I found the episode balanced. However, I would add one doubt: not everybody has a quiet room at home, so the benefits may be smaller for some people. I see her point, but I would like to hear more before I decide. In short, the episode was clear and useful, and I agree with her up to a point.
accepted: In this episode, the host asked her guest whether it is better to work from home. According to the guest, it depends. Third, she said that companies could offer two office days a week, which she described as a good compromise. When the host asked whether working at home is better, she answered that it is not exactly better, which seemed to imply that the answer is not a simple yes. What struck me was that she never said it is easy. To be fair, I found the episode balanced. However, I would add one doubt: not everybody has a quiet room at home, so the benefits may be smaller for some people. I see her point, but I would like to hear more before I decide. In short, the episode was clear and useful, and I agree with her up to a point.

This episode of the podcast was about working from home. The host asked her guest if it is better, and the guest explained that it depends. On the positive side, many people save two hours a day because they do not travel to an office. On the negative side, some of them feel lonely and hardly see their colleagues. She suggested that a good compromise could be two office days a week. The host asked again whether working at home is better, and the guest replied not exactly, which implied that the situation is more complicated than a simple yes or no. My reaction is positive: to be fair, she did not try to sell one answer. What struck me was how honest she was about the problems. However, I would add that some people do not have a quiet place at home, and that could make things harder for them. Overall, I agree with her up to a point, and I would like to hear how companies respond.

feedback.es: El texto resume lo dicho con fidelidad, detecta la implicación de «not exactly», reacciona con matiz y cierra con una conclusión.

origin.text: Escucha el episodio (puedes oírlo varias veces) y escribe en inglés, de 160 a 300 palabras, una reseña: resume las ideas de la invitada (atribúyelas), señala una implicación, añade tu reacción con un matiz (to be fair, I would add…) y termina con una frase de cierre. No inventes datos.
origin.audio: Host: Welcome to the show. Today my guest studies working from home. Is it better to work at home? Guest: Well, it depends. Many people save two hours a day because they do not travel, and that is a real benefit. Host: So it is better? Guest: Not exactly. Some people tell me they feel lonely, and they hardly see their colleagues. Host: Is there a solution? Guest: Perhaps. Companies could offer two office days a week, and I suppose that is a good compromise. Host: Thank you for joining us.
